text:
Pavel Zacha is having the kind of season that makes a decision harder. He has 12 points in 16 games playing 19 minutes a night beside David Pastrnak (Daily Faceoff ranked them among the league's elite duos), and he is in the last year of his contract. The Hockey Writers and Heavy.com are already asking whether Boston should trade him now or pay him later.

His own numbers are sound. Five goals on 4.17 expected is close to fair, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 86th percentile among forwards for chances from in front of the net last season, with 60 percent of his entries carried in. A 6'4" center who gets to the net and exits the zone cleanly is worth something to every contender.

The caution flag is on-ice luck: the Bruins have scored 9.2 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and their five-on-five share is worse with him than without. Some of the assists will fade. Our projection lands around 71 points if he plays out the season in Boston, and that "if" is the story to watch.
headline: Zacha is producing in a contract year
